summary.text: Atoms are the basic building blocks of matter, each made of a nucleus of protons and generally neutrons with a swarm of electrons around it.
The number of protons sets which element an atom is, and equal numbers of protons and electrons leave the atom neutral.
A human hair is about a million carbon atoms wide, and more than 99.94% of an atom's mass is in its nucleus.

facts.label: Mass location
facts.value: More than 99.94% sits in the nucleus

facts.label: 11 protons
facts.value: Any atom with 11 protons is sodium

facts.label: 29 protons
facts.value: Any atom with 29 protons is copper

items.prompt: A neutral atom picks up one extra electron. What does it become?

options.label: A positively charged ion, or cation
A negatively charged ion, or anion
An isotope of the same element
An atom of a different element

items.explain: More electrons than protons gives an overall negative charge, which is called a negative ion.

items.prompt: Why don't an atom's electrons simply drift away from it?

options.label: Opposite charges: negative electrons, positive nucleus
The nuclear force reaching out to pull them in
Neutrons sitting between them and holding them
Gravity from the protons gripping each of them

items.explain: The electrons are negative and the nucleus is positive, and this opposing charge binds them.

items.prompt: Inside a nucleus, the electric push between protons grows stronger than the force holding it together. What happens?

options.label: The nucleus gains extra electrons
The atom becomes a different isotope
The protons swap places with neutrons
The nucleus splits and leaves different elements behind

items.explain: When the repelling electromagnetic force beats the nuclear force, the nucleus splits, a form of nuclear decay.

items.prompt: Why can't a microscope that uses ordinary light ever show you a single atom?

options.label: Atoms move too quickly to focus on
Atoms are transparent to every kind of light
Atoms are smaller than the shortest wavelength of visible light
Atoms are held too tightly in molecules

items.explain: Atoms are smaller than the shortest wavelength of visible light, so conventional microscopes cannot show them.

items.prompt: A chemist compares several compounds that all contain the same two elements. The amount of one element per fixed amount of the other differs by small whole-number ratios. What did Dalton conclude?

options.label: Each element can be split without limit
Each element combines in multiples of a basic unit of weight
Compounds change their makeup as they cool
All elements share one common unit of weight

items.explain: The pattern suggested each element has a unique basic unit of weight, which Dalton called atoms.

items.prompt: Ancient thinkers proposed tiny indivisible particles. What did Dalton add in the early 1800s?

options.label: A new name for the same philosophical idea
Proof that the particles could be cut in half
A way to see the particles under a microscope
Experimental evidence that matter comes in discrete units

items.explain: The old ideas rested on philosophical reasoning, while Dalton found evidence that matter is made of discrete units.
